target_moa.text: Naldemedine is an opioid antagonist with binding affinities for mu-, delta-, and kappa-opioid receptors that functions as a peripherally-acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist (PAMORA) in tissues such as the GI tract, decreasing the constipating effects of opioids.

citations.quote: Nalmedemine is an opioid antagonist with binding affinities for mu-, delta-, and kappa-opioid receptors. Nalmedemine functions as a peripherally-acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist in tissues such as the gastrointestinal tract, thereby decreasing the constipating effects of opioids.

Use of opioids induces slowing of gastrointestinal motility and transit. Antagonism of gastrointestinal mu-opioid receptors by naldemedine inhibits opioid-induced delay of gastrointestinal transit time.

modality.text: Small molecule (oral opioid antagonist; derivative of naltrexone)

citations.quote: Naldemedine, a new molecular entity, is a derivative of naltrexone. It is an antagonist of opioid binding to mu-, delta-, and kappa-opioid receptors.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=2%) are abdominal pain, diarrhea, and nausea. In pooled Studies 1 and 2: abdominal pain 8% vs 2% placebo, diarrhea 7% vs 2%, nausea 4% vs 2%. Opioid withdrawal occurred in ~1% of subjects. GI perforation and opioid withdrawal are warnings.
